description: Scribe of the Chronicle — the book in your hands. She began it the day her grief went missing, and she will not close it until she knows what took it.
lore: Britt was the younger by six years and the quicker by every measure that is fun at a fair, and the sisters sang in parts — Britt above, Bettany under — through every wash-day of two lifetimes, the living one and this one. What happened when Britt went on is told in [[lore/the_long_morning|the Long Morning]], and Bettany would rather you read it there. The short of it: everyone the going-on bereaves loses the grief itself, and everyone but her has agreed to call that mercy.

In the back of [[lore/the_chronicle|the Chronicle]], past the last written page, there is a private column of dates. On Britt's day each year Bettany sings both parts of the wash-song alone, her line and then her sister's — she has lost none of it, which is the whole horror — and waits to feel anything at all, and writes the result beside the date. The column is longer now than some chapters. Every entry says: still nothing. She is a careful scribe. If it ever says something else, she wants to know the day.

She interviews everyone who will sit, and most sit once. [[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] gets her a whole evening every week and believes it is for his east road, which she has duly saved — forty pages, milestone by milestone. She keeps coming for a different reason. Wendell met Britt once, at a shearing, and he tells it a little differently each time — the dress, the weather, what Britt called across the pen — and Bettany sits very still through every version, waiting for the one with something new in it. He knows exactly what he is doing. He spins that morning out a thread a week, because the evenings are what he is really trading for; she pays, and both of them let the price go on being called the road.
gm_notes: Carries B8 (revealed): the missing grief is stated as a phenomenon she measures, never explained. B9 — that the goer carries the grief out — stays HIDDEN; the still-nothing column is her instrument for it and must never contain its answer. New leaf-canon: the back-column ritual, and Wendell rationing his one Britt memory to buy her company — a gentle mutual lie that characterises both. Her authorship of the wiki is established in the_chronicle; this record stays personal.
